summary: EDNS client-subnet rewrite by on-prem DNS forwarder causes control-plane region misroute and TLS cert name mismatch on private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
FluxAnalytics reported intermittent failures for control-plane operations and model shard fetches from their private deployment in us-west-2. Failures present as short-lived control-plane timeouts, followed by TLS certificate name mismatch errors on artifact fetches and some presigned URL 403s.

Impact:
- Customers' production inference routes intermittently fail (5-10% of requests) for ~30-90s windows.
- Observed during peak traffic; customers see degraded tail latency and occasional 5xx from SDKs.

Environment:
- Customer: FluxAnalytics (private deployment, VPC peering to Redwood transit VPC).
- Region: us-west-2.
- Nodes: private control-plane behind VPCE; serving nodes in customer's VPC.
- Private DNS: on-prem forwarder -> customer egress -> upstream resolver chain (reseller DNS + regional CDN GeoDNS).

Steps to reproduce:
1) From serving node in customer's VPC, resolve control-plane hostname repeatedly (dig +short) and observe A/AAAA answers over time.
2) Simultaneously tail control-plane TLS handshake logs and SDK errors.
3) Run dig +edns @<customer-forwarder> <control-plane-hostname> +short and dig +trace to observe EDNS client-subnet behavior.

Observed logs / outputs (excerpts):
- SDK error: "tls: certificate is not valid for requested name: controlplane.us-west-2.private.redwood.net (got cert for controlplane-eu-west.redwood-cdn.example.com)"
- Serving node syslog: "fetch shard: presigned GET https://s3-us-west-2.redwood... -> 403 signature mismatch"
- dig @10.1.4.2 controlplane.private.redwood.net +short -> 13.32.11.97 / 2600:1f18:xxxx::1
- repeated dig after ~40s -> 52.17.4.23 / 2a03:xxxx::23 (eu-west range)

Initial hypothesis:
On-prem DNS forwarder is rewriting EDNS Client Subnet (ECS) or otherwise normalizing the client subnet to an IP that maps to a different region in upstream GeoDNS. This causes the control-plane hostname to resolve to an external/cdn-backed endpoint in the wrong region intermittently. The client then attempts TLS to that IP and fails because the certificate presented matches the CDN host name not the expected private hostname, and presigned artifact URLs (which are region-bound) fail or return 403s when routed to the wrong origin.

Immediate customer impact: control-plane auth loops and model fetches fail until DNS answers stabilize.

Requested action: full root-cause investigation and mitigation steps + temporary workaround to restore stability while customer remediate on-prem DNS behavior.
comments: 2026-03-10 15:12 - Support (Aisha): Received initial report from FluxAnalytics. Customer noticing short 30-90s windows of control-plane auth failures. Asked for dig +trace output and SDK logs.

2026-03-10 15:45 - Customer (Ops Lead, Maya R.): Attached dig +trace and tcpdump from a serving node. Noting the IP answers flip between us-west and eu-west ranges. Can we route around until we fix our forwarder?
2026-03-10 17:10 - Support (Aisha): Confirmed certificate commonName observed belongs to a CDN edge (eu-west). Escalated to SRE. Opened temporary bypass guidance (hosts entry) while investigating.

2026-03-10 19:04 - SRE (Tomás): Ran parallel dig against customer forwarder and directly to upstream resolver. Found EDNS0 ECS option being rewritten to a /24 that maps to EU. Packet captures show on-prem forwarder rewrites client-subnet. Created pcap snapshot and uploaded to ticket.

2026-03-11 09:12 - Customer: We scheduled network team to check the forwarder; they reported a managed reseller appliance doing ECS normalization for privacy. Asking whether Redwood can prefer IPv4 or validate certname earlier to avoid falling back to wrong endpoint.

2026-03-12 11:23 - SRE: Implemented and tested a conservative fallback in staging to prefer IPv4 addresses when TLS cert name mismatch is detected and to re-query control-plane via alternative resolvers before failing. Not yet in prod; testing ongoing.

2026-03-13 08:43 - Support (Aisha): Customer applied a temporary /etc/hosts override for control-plane on a subset of nodes and reported stability improved over the previous 24h window. Work with customer network team on permanent disable of ECS rewrite or configured split-dns at forwarder.
2026-03-13 14:57 - Customer (Maya): Network team plans to deploy forwarder config change to stop ECS normalization; ETA 2026-03-15. Please keep ticket open until we confirm no recurrence.
investigation_notes: Checked DNS answers over a 2 hour window: answers oscillate between IP blocks belonging to us-west-2 and eu-west-1 (ASNs differ).

tcpdump on serving node shows DNS queries leaving to 10.1.4.2 (customer forwarder) with EDNS0 present. Upstream responses reflect client-subnet /24 originating from forwarder, not the actual node source IP.
TLS handshake logs show sni=controlplane.private.redwood.net but presented certificate CN contains controlplane-eu-west.redwood-cdn.example.com, causing verify error.
Presigned URL requests forwarded to wrong CDN edge produced 403 from S3 due to region mismatch and signature host mismatch (signature V4 region-bound).
Tested resolving via 8.8.8.8 and cloud-resolver; always returned US-west addresses. Resolving via customer forwarder intermittently returned EU addresses.
Temporary workaround (hosts override) stabilizes control-plane connections; indicates DNS answer is root cause rather than routing/GW flapping.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation provided: 1) Hosts-file override on serving nodes for control-plane host to pin to us-west-2 control-plane IPs; 2) Customer network team to disable EDNS Client Subnet normalization on their forwarder (reseller appliance).

Longer-term mitigations: 1) We will add a control-plane resolver fallback to detect geo-drift by validating certificate commonName vs requested host and re-querying via known-good resolvers before promoting error to client. 2) Add telemetry to detect EDNS-originated geo-drift and alert automatically.
Customer confirmed front-line stability after hosts override; they will roll forwarder config change on 2026-03-15 and monitor for recurrence. Keep ticket open until 2026-03-18 for verification.
Assigned internal follow-up: INT-21402 to add EDNS drift detection and retry logic in control-plane client library (owners: control-plane team).
root_cause: On-prem DNS forwarder normalizes/rewrites EDNS Client Subnet to a range located in a different region. Upstream GeoDNS uses ECS to return region-specific endpoints so some queries resolved to eu-west CDN edges, causing TLS certname mismatch and region-bound presigned URL failures.
next_steps: SRE: deploy certname validation + re-resolve fallback to prod routing library (target 2026-03-20).
Support: keep ticket open and monitor customer telemetry until 2026-03-18.
Customer: apply forwarder config change to stop ECS normalization (in progress, ETA 2026-03-15).
ENG: INT-21402 to implement EDNS-drift metric and auto-retry logic (owner: control-plane team).
